source.title: Competency-based education for CBSE — Item Bank: Science Class 8 (September 2021)
source.subject: science
source.authorityName: Central Board of Secondary Education (content created by the British Council)
source.usage: Official CBSE item bank, freely available on cbseacademic.nic.in for teachers to use as they wish; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.
source.notes: A bank of 36 practice items (not an examination paper) for Science Class 8, published by CBSE in September 2021 with content created by the British Council; each item has metadata (AO marks, content reference, marks), optional source material, questions and a mark scheme (Answer / Guidance), from which officialAnswer is taken. Items are not numbered in the document (each item's question is numbered '1'), so `number` is the item identity printed at the top of each item (e.g. 'Science8VS6') and `part` is the printed sub-part label. Items map to the NCERT books current in 2021; chapters were mapped by topic to the current NCERT Class 8 book and must be confirmed. Topics with no chapter in the current book (fibres, crop production, reproduction in animals, combustion/flame/fuels, sound) have chapter null. Several items print a total that disagrees with their part marks (GS3, GS5, JS3, RB2); part marks from the item metadata were used. Introduction, item index, assessment objectives and metadata tables were skipped.

questions.text: Addition of salt a is a well-known method of food preservation. Explain how it prevents food spoilage.

officialAnswer.text: Salt draws out water from the cells of the food and bacteria through the process of osmosis. (1) The growth of bacteria is prohibited due to the absence of an optimum amount of water. (1) Guidance: The cells of the food and bacteria lose water through osmosis due to difference in concentration of salt. Bacteria needs optimum water, temperature and air to grow. (1)

questions.text: Justify with the help of two examples that microorganisms can be beneficial for humans.

(1) Some bacteria and fungi are used to produce antibiotics eg Streptomycin. (1) Production of vaccines (1) Rhizobium bacteria fixes atmospheric Nitrogen. (1) Microorganisms are decomposers and thus help in cleaning the environment. (1) Guidance: (Any two valid points, 1 point for each point)

questions.text: FRICTION - Any object, moving over the surface of another objects slows down when no external force is applied on it. If force is applied along the left, friction acts along the right. The force of friction always opposes the applied force. Friction is caused by the irregularities on the two surfaces in contact. The force of friction is greater if a rough surface is involved. Explain using ideas of friction why it is difficult to move on a wet marble floor.

officialAnswer.text: On a wet marble floor, frictional force between the foot and floor decreases making it slippery, thus we feel difficult to move on a wet marble floor. (1) Guidance: Rolling friction is smaller than all the given frictions. (1 Mark)

questions.text: A metal block was allowed to drop from the same height onto different wooden blocks of same mass but different contact area. Using your knowledge of pressure, explain the relationship between the contact area of the wooden block and how deep the wooden block would sink into the soft ground?
extractionIssues: The mark scheme has an extra first part 1(a) (predicting how deep a block of contact area 9.0 cm2 would sink, answer 5.1 cm) that refers to results not printed in the question; the scheme's labels are shifted by one (this part is scheme 1(b))

officialAnswer.text: As Pressure is equal to force divided by area, hence as the contact area of the wooden block increases, the depth to which block would sink into the soft ground decreases. (2 mark) Guidance: Accept Pressure= Force/ Area (1) The area of the wooden block increases, the depth to which it will sink decreases. (1) Also accept – If the area of the wooden block decreases the depth to which it will sink increases.

(1) Recycling metal uses less energy than smelting ore to create new metals.
